text:
Sam: hey folks — landing my first runtime PR and hitting a few bumps. quick onboarding questions: what branch name style do we use? who normally reviews eng-runtime changes? pre-commit keeps failing for me with black/ruff errors and i don't know the config to match. any short checklist?

Maya: welcome! :tada: branch pattern we prefer is `feat/<ticket>-short-desc` or `fix/<ticket>-short-desc` for small patches. for infra/runtime stuff we sometimes use `chore/` if it's non-user-facing.

Maya: reviewers: if it's runtime performance/serving-code, ping @Olivia and add reviewer team `eng-runtime-reviewers`. if it's router/orchestration, ping @Ryan. add label `area/runtime`.

Maya: for pre-commit, try these locally:
```bash
# from repo root
poetry install  # or use your venv
poetry run pre-commit install
poetry run pre-commit run --all-files
make ci-lint   # runs ruff/black/isort according to our config
```

Ryan: small tip — keep the runtime change separate from any refactors. split into 2 PRs if possible: one for the behavioral change and one for cleanup. smaller PRs = faster reviews.

ci-bot: CI status: FAILED — flake8 error in `inference/runtime/kernels.py: line 142` (E501 line too long). Full logs: https://ci.example.com/builds/8721

Sam: ah thanks — saw that. i pushed a fix to wrap the long string and ran `poetry run pre-commit run --all-files` locally, but CI still complained about an import order. guessing isort mismatch.

Maya: run `make ci-lint` — our isort settings are in `pyproject.toml`. If you want, paste the failing snippet and i can paste the exact isort command. also remember to run `git commit --no-verify` only if pre-commit blockers are CI false-positives (rare).

Olivia: also, add a short test or a smoke check if you're changing kernels. We try to keep at least one unit test per behavioral change in `tests/runtime/`. Run a single test with:
```bash
poetry run pytest tests/runtime/test_kernels.py::test_example -q
```

Olivia: feel free to draft the PR and mark it `WIP` — reviewers will take a look. tag me and @Ryan for an early review pass.

Sam: awesome — pushed the isort fix and added a small smoke test. created PR `#4821` and assigned to Olivia+Ryan. thanks for the quick orientation, this helps a lot :relieved:

Ryan: nice! quick checklist to include in PR description: short summary, perf expectations, what changed, how to test locally, which benchmarks to run (if any), and rollout plan (canary/rollback).

Sam: adding that now. one last q: is there a label for performance-sensitive changes?

Maya: use `perf-sensitive` + `area/runtime`. we'll surface it in the release notes if needed.

Sam: perfect, thanks all!
